reason: Start splitting the water by collecting hydrogen at its outlet.
expectation: I expect a supply of hydrogen for the fuel plant; I am unsure whether oxygen is collected simultaneously.

alternatives.reason: Capturing carbon dioxide also advances a goal, but I want to start with the water split.

effect: Hydrogen is available separately; I still need to collect oxygen.
reaction: The result is straightforward, though it does not explain whether the other gas was produced at the same time.
reason: Collect oxygen to finish separating the water.
expectation: I expect an oxygen supply and completion of the water-separation goal.

alternatives.reason: Carbon dioxide capture is another goal, but I want to finish the water route first.

effect: Both gases are now collected and the separation goal is complete.
reaction: The two separate outlet actions felt a little repetitive, but their purpose was clear.
reason: Capture carbon dioxide for the remaining goal; it is the only gameplay action offered.
expectation: The receiver will collect compressed carbon dioxide, though compression might require another step.

effect: The receiver captures and compresses carbon dioxide in one action, completing the chapter.
reaction: I was surprised it ended here; I expected to see the gases used to fill the lander tanks.

mostWorthwhile.text: Collecting hydrogen and oxygen linked the water supply to the return plant, an appealing reuse of something already made.

leastWorthwhile.text: The two outlet actions felt repetitive: each produced a named supply without showing much about the separation.

surprise.text: Capturing carbon dioxide completed the chapter before any fuel-making or tank-filling action appeared.

arbitrary.text: The separate water-to-outlet actions made sense as collection, though I was unsure how they represented one water-splitting process.

continue.text: Yes, I would continue to see how the captured gases become propellant and connect to the journey home; this short chapter alone felt more like setup than a satisfying construction.
